title: Parliament approves maximum grant for Sudan debt relief via IMF trust
what_it_is: A motion under section 6A(2)(d) of the Bretton Woods Agreements Act 1966, moved by Minister of State for Trade and Industry Alvin Tan on behalf of the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister-in-charge of the Monetary Authority of Singapore, setting the maximum amount MAS may give under a bilateral agreement with the International Monetary Fund to support Sudan's debt relief efforts.
why_it_matters: The resolution caps the grant that the Monetary Authority of Singapore may give under a bilateral agreement with the International Monetary Fund at 4,480,000 Special Drawing Rights (approximately US$6,100,000). The money is to support Sudan's debt relief efforts via the Trust for Special Poverty Reduction and Growth Operations for the Heavily Indebted Poor Countries. The record does not set out further practical impact for people in Singapore.

key_points.point: Alvin Tan moved that Parliament resolve the maximum grant MAS may give under a bilateral agreement with the IMF to support Sudan's debt relief efforts is 4,480,000 Special Drawing Rights (approximately US$6,100,000).
